methods.rationale: Applies typical Growth → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $47M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Drones & Autonomous (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 7 same-sector peers exist in Drones & Autonomous, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Pivotal, a Growth-stage drone and autonomous systems company founded by Marcus Leng, operates within a sector containing seven identifiable private peers including Waymo, Wayve, Zipline, Joby Aviation, and Nuro. No public comparables exist in the narrow peer set, limiting cross-market validation. The company has raised capital backing from Page.

The valuation analysis applies a single applicable method: Stage-Progression. Using total capital raised of approximately $47M as a base proxy, application of a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical for Growth-to-next-stage progression yields an implied value of $56M. A peer-median approach was not viable; while seven same-sector peers exist, none met minimum thresholds for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier matching—requiring at least three datapoints—making sector-wide medians unreliable.

The triangulated analysis, constrained to one method, suggests a valuation range of $48M (low) to $64M (high), with a median point of $56M. This range reflects stage-typical step-up dynamics rather than market-comparative anchoring. The single-method constraint and absence of narrowly comparable Growth-stage transactions in drones and autonomous systems introduce material uncertainty. Valuation tightening would require either disclosure of comparable recent rounds in this subsector or expansion of acceptable peer criteria. Investors should treat this as illustrative of order of magnitude pending additional comp availability or transaction data.
